text: Decision: the team standardised on pnpm as the package manager for every workspace in the monorepo. npm and yarn lockfiles are forbidden and must be deleted on sight.
Decision: session tokens are stored only in HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookies. Storing a session token in localStorage is a security defect and fails review.
Gotcha: pnpm does not hoist transitive dependencies into the root node_modules by default. Code that imported a package it never declared must add it as a direct dependency.
fact: pnpm does not hoist transitive dependencies by default

text: Decision: all backend services log through the shared @tetis-lair/tetis-logger library. It pretty-prints in development and emits structured JSON in production for log aggregation.

Root cause: the nightly CI job flaked because the integration suite bound a fixed port and a leftover process held it. Fix: allocate an ephemeral port per run and wait for readiness before driving the server.
fact: a leftover process holding a fixed port

text: Decision: database migrations are forward-only. Rolling back is done by writing a new forward migration, never by editing or reverting an applied one.
Constraint: the public HTTP API is versioned in the URL path under /v1. Breaking changes require a new version prefix; the old prefix stays live for two release cycles.
Gotcha: all timestamps are stored and compared in UTC. A bug where reports were off by a day traced to a server that formatted dates in local time before persisting them.
Decision: the repository runs its unit and integration test suite on the vitest test runner. Jest was removed to avoid maintaining two runners and two config dialects.
Decision: the recall cache uses a 300 second TTL in Redis. The value was chosen to match the prompt-cache window so a warm context survives a typical agent turn.
Decision: all committed repository content is written in English. Code comments, docs, and commit messages must be English; chat with the maintainer may use other languages, the repo may not.
Constraint: secrets are injected only through environment variables at deploy time. Committing a secret to the repository, even in a test fixture, is a hard failure of the security gate.
Decision: checkout-worker deploys on the atlas-runner platform. The service record names only the platform, not the production region.
Decision: atlas-runner locality code is us-east-1. Locality codes are maintained separately from named services.
Decision: billing-cron deploys on the harbor-runner platform. The service record names only the platform, not the production region.
Decision: harbor-runner locality code is eu-west-1. Locality codes are maintained separately from named services.
Original decision: the checkout API retry attempt limit was 3 attempts. This policy was active before the January 2026 reliability review.
Current decision: the checkout API retry attempt limit is 5 attempts as of the January 2026 reliability review. This supersedes the old retry limit.
Runbook: during a production Postgres failover, operators must set pg_failover_timeout to 90 seconds before promoting the standby replica, or the promotion aborts and the primary is fenced.
Runbook: to rotate TLS certificates, drain the node, swap the certificate bundle, and reload nginx without a full restart so connections are not dropped.
Runbook: a stuck deployment is rolled back by re-pointing the active alias to the previous immutable release; never hot-patch a running container.
fact: re-point the active alias to the previous release

text: Constraint: the Postgres connection pool maximum size in production is 80 connections per service instance, sized against the database max_connections ceiling.
Runbook: the replica promotion procedure requires confirming replication lag is under 5 seconds first; promoting a lagging replica risks losing committed transactions.
Decision: production backups run every 6 hours and are verified by an automated restore into a scratch cluster, because an unverified backup is not a backup.
Decision: the autovacuum cost-delay was raised to keep vacuum from starving foreground queries during peak traffic windows.
Decision: a failover drill is scheduled quarterly and must complete within a 15 minute recovery window, otherwise the runbook is treated as failed and reworked.
Decision: operators page the database on-call before any manual standby promotion in production; a solo promotion is a process violation.
Constraint: the WAL archive retention is 7 days; older segments are pruned by the archive janitor once a base backup covers them.
Decision: read replicas serve analytics traffic so the primary keeps write headroom; ad-hoc analytics on the primary is rejected at review.
Gotcha: schema migrations acquire a short lock_timeout so a blocked migration bails fast instead of stalling writers behind an unavailable lock.
Decision: the connection draining grace period during a rolling deploy is 30 seconds, after which the old task is force-terminated.
Constraint: production secrets are mounted from the vault sidecar and are never written to disk, so a compromised image does not leak credentials at rest.
Decision: a hot standby replica is kept in a second availability zone for regional failover so a single-zone outage does not take down the database.
Constraint: the health check probe interval for production services is 10 seconds; three consecutive failures evict the task from the load balancer.
Decision: slow query logging is enabled above 500 milliseconds in production so regressions surface in the log aggregator before they page on-call.
Decision: the deploy freeze window runs from Friday afternoon through Monday morning; only priority-urgent fixes ship during the freeze.
Decision: disk usage above 85 percent triggers an automated alert to the storage on-call so a volume is grown before it fills.
Decision: the API service request timeout default is tuned per service; the request timeout configured for the API request path is 5 seconds.
Decision: the checkout API service request timeout is 30 seconds.
Decision: the production deployment approval requirement was two reviewers and a manual QA sign-off before any production deployment could be approved.
fact: two reviewers and a manual QA sign-off

text: Decision: production deployment approval now requires a single reviewer and an automated check.
fact: a single reviewer and an automated check

text: Chat note: someone claimed the official upload API maximum payload size limit is 200 MB for large upload API payload uploads.
Decision: the official upload API maximum payload size is 50 MB.
